source_text:
Χειροτονήσατε οὖν ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισκόπους καὶ διακόνους ἀξίους τοῦ κυρίου, ἄνδρας πραεῖς καὶ ἀφιλαργύρους καὶ ἀληθεῖς καὶ δεδοκιμασμένους: ὑμῖν γὰρ λειτουργοῦσι καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν λειτουργίαν τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων.
μὴ οὖν ὑπερίδητε αὐτούς: αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ τετιμημένοι ὑμῶν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων.
Ἐλέγχετε δὲ ἀλλήλους μὴ ἐν ὀργῇ, ἀλλ’ ἐν εἰρήνῃ ὡς ἔχετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ: καὶ παντὶ ἀστοχοῦντι κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου μηδεὶς λαλείτω μηδὲ παῤ ὑμῶν ἀκουέτω, ἕως οὗ μετανοήσῃ.
τὰς δὲ εὐχὰς ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς ἐλεημοσύνας καὶ πάσας τὰς πράξεις οὕτω ποιήσατε, ὡς ἔχετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
thought_title: Appoint worthy leaders and correct one another in peace
orientation: The community is being instructed on how to order its common life: appointing local leaders, honoring them, and practicing mutual correction.
pass_a_gloss: Appoint therefore for yourselves bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men gentle and not-loving-money and true and tested: for to you they minister and they themselves the ministry of the prophets and teachers. Do not therefore overlook them: for they themselves are the honored ones of you with the prophets and teachers. Correct but one another not in anger, but in peace as you have in the gospel: and to everyone missing the mark against the other let no one speak nor from you let him hear, until he repents. The but prayers of you and the alms and all the deeds thus do, as you have in the gospel of the Lord of us.

choices.why: The verb means to choose or appoint by a show of hands or vote; 'appoint' fits the community context without implying a specific modern ordination rite.
The compound adjective is negated 'loving money'; keeping the negation explicit preserves the source's force.
The perfect participle means 'having been put to the test and approved'; 'tested' captures both the process and the result.
The verb is cognate with the noun 'ministry' in the same clause; 'minister' preserves the wordplay and the sense of service.
The verb means to overlook or despise; 'look down on' captures the dismissive attitude the text warns against.
The verb means to miss the mark or fail; in context it refers to wrongdoing against another person, so 'wrongs' is the clearest rendering.

pass_b_english: So appoint for yourselves bishops and deacons who are worthy of the Lord—men who are gentle, not money-loving, truthful, and tested. For they also minister to you the ministry of the prophets and teachers.
Do not look down on them, then, for they are your honored ones, along with the prophets and teachers.
Correct one another not in anger but in peace, as you have it in the gospel. And if anyone wrongs another, let no one speak to him or hear anything from him until he repents.
Perform your prayers, your acts of mercy, and all your deeds just as you have it in the gospel of our Lord.
